clue.text: Just where to hit the hay!

definitions.text: Just where to hit the hay!

blocks.clueFragment: Just where to hit the hay!
blocks.note: surface reading: simply the place to go to bed and get some sleep
setter's reading: the bed itself is stuffed with straw, so you are literally lying on the hay

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit the hay' is slang for going to bed; the joke is that this particular bed is filled with straw.
explanation.definitionFit: A palliasse is an old-fashioned straw-filled mattress, so sleeping on one is lying on hay.

clue.text: Faced the camera, showing tranquillity. Not I

indicators.note: the instruction says one letter, the letter I, is to be left out of the word found

blocks.note: someone poised shows calm composure
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sitter keeps calm while being photographed, with a strange afterthought about not themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To pose is to hold a position for a photographer or painter.

clue.text: Sheltered area where diesel is spilt at end of lane

indicators.note: spilt fuel runs everywhere, so its letters scatter into a new order
only the final letter of the following word is wanted

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of lane

explanation.surface: A lay-by beside a country lane where a lorry has leaked fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: The lee side of something is the side away from the wind, so it is sheltered.

clue.text: No matter where and how you pack — whatever!

definitions.text: No matter where and how you pack

blocks.clueFragment: No matter where and how you pack
blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: inside some piece of luggage or other
second meaning: regardless, anyway

explanation.walkthrough: The first half treats a case as a suitcase; the second is the everyday phrase meaning 'regardless'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for 'anyway, regardless of circumstances', matching a dismissive 'whatever'.

clue.text: Petty to conceal TV

blocks.note: petty means small-minded or trivial
to screen something is to hide it from view

explanation.surface: Accusing someone of being mean-spirited for hiding the television.
explanation.definitionFit: Television is commonly called the small screen, in contrast to the cinema's big screen.

clue.text: Priest met Old Vic central characters

indicators.note: only the letter in the very centre of each of the next words is kept

blocks.note: the middle letter of met
the middle letter of Old
the middle letter of Vic

explanation.surface: A clergyman meets the leading actors at the Old Vic, a famous London theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central characters' suggests star actors, but it means the middle letters of three short words.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli is the Old Testament priest who brought up the boy Samuel, a crossword regular.

clue.text: Give address that's fancy, not new

indicators.note: says a letter is to be taken away from the word just found

blocks.note: fancy decoration is ornate
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Advice to a speaker to make a showy speech without novelty.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech, which is giving an address.

clue.text: Primarily, observed aquatic source in Sahara

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A traveller spots water in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the initials spell the word and the words describe it.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert where water comes to the surface.

clue.text: Meandering road ran up in the Pyrenees

definitions.note: describes where the country is rather than naming it

indicators.note: something meandering wanders off its course, so these letters wander into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A winding mountain road climbs into the Pyrenees.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a tiny principality high in the Pyrenees between France and Spain.

clue.text: Wheels turned before reaching a different location

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adverb meaning 'in a different place'

indicators.note: something turned is moved round, so these letters change their order

blocks.note: taken as written
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A car's wheels turn before it arrives somewhere new.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsewhere means in or to some other place.

clue.text: Composer from Naples met an Austrian

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of a run of the words that follow

blocks.note: letters straddling the words, from the end of Naples to the start of Austrian

explanation.surface: A musician from Naples meets someone from Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composer from Naples' looks like an Italian composer; 'from' is the signal and Naples is just part of the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana was a Czech composer, best known for Má vlast.

clue.text: Fashionable teams showing guts?

blocks.note: something in is in fashion
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: Stylish teams demonstrating courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guts' reads as courage; here it means the internal organs.
explanation.definitionFit: Insides is an informal word for the stomach and bowels, the same as guts.

clue.text: Girl in chains?

definitions.note: the flower found in a daisy chain, a loose cryptic hint rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: a girl's first name
second meaning: a flower that children thread together into chains

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a captive in shackles; the question mark flags that the chains are made of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The name doubles as a small white-petalled lawn flower famously strung into chains by children.

clue.text: Breaking point for injured stalwarts

indicators.note: injured things are knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Losing loyal players to injury is when the team finally cracks.
explanation.definitionFit: The last straw, from the straw that broke the camel's back, is the final thing that makes something unbearable.

clue.text: Ones learning about rites in Mass

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the following letters are turned into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Trainees studying the rituals of the Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'concerning' but signals the rearrangement; 'in' belongs to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Seminarists are students at a seminary, training to be priests.

clue.text: President miles away from VP Pence

indicators.note: something away from a word is no longer in it, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for miles
Mike Pence was US vice-president

explanation.surface: A president keeps far from his vice-president.
explanation.definitionFit: Ike was the nickname of Dwight D. Eisenhower, US president 1953 to 1961.

clue.text: Unwilling?

blocks.note: surface reading: reluctant, not wanting to do something
setter's reading: un-will-ing, lacking a legal will at death

explanation.walkthrough: Split the word as 'without a will' and it describes someone who dies leaving no testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone intestate has died without making a valid will.

clue.text: Oblige with lodgings?

blocks.note: first meaning: do someone a favour, fit in with their wishes
second meaning: house someone, provide them with lodgings

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is read as 'provide with lodgings'; the question mark flags the loose phrasing.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to help someone out and to provide somewhere to stay.

clue.text: Persistent occupation of old boy, sitting

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a sitting of a court or parliament is a session

explanation.surface: A former pupil whose long-term job is sitting down.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession occupies the mind persistently, a fixation.

clue.text: Sport memorial by Irish county town

blocks.note: a commemorative plaque is a tablet
Ennis is the county town of Clare in Ireland

explanation.surface: A sporting memorial stands beside an Irish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Table tennis, or ping-pong, is a sport played with bats on a table.

clue.text: Hunting dogs and black birds

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
eagles are birds

explanation.surface: A hunting scene with dogs and dark birds overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black birds' looks like blackbirds or crows; black is a single letter and the birds are separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Beagles are small hounds bred for hunting hares.

clue.text: Extra portion from Derby executive

indicators.note: a portion is a piece cut out of the following words

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of Derby and the start of executive

explanation.surface: An extra slice of something from a businessman in Derby, an English Midlands city.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored without the batter hitting the ball, counted as an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A bye is one of the cricket extras, runs not credited to any batter.

clue.text: Midlander starts broadcasting game, we hear

indicators.note: only the starting letter of the following word is used
says the result is spoken, so the spelling may differ

blocks.note: the first letter of broadcasting
rummy is a card game

explanation.surface: Someone from the Midlands begins commentating on a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Brummie is slang for a person from Birmingham, England's second city in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brummie comes from Birmingham, so is a Midlander.

clue.text: Shopkeeper bursts into tears

indicators.note: bursting breaks something apart, so the letters fly into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper suddenly starts crying.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'bursts into tears' reads as one idiom, but 'bursts' is the signal and the rest are the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer runs a shop selling paper, pens and other writing materials.

clue.text: Moon looking pale from Des Moines?

blocks.note: Io is a moon of Jupiter
wan means pale and sickly-looking

explanation.surface: The moon looks pale when seen from an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Des Moines is the capital of Iowa, so a person from there is from that state.

clue.text: Last of rowers having to cut down blade

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is wanted

blocks.note: the last letter of rowers
to cull is to reduce numbers by killing

explanation.surface: The final rower in the boat must shorten an oar.
explanation.definitionFit: A scull is a light oar, and its flat end is called the blade.

clue.text: Ghastly clue and grids inside

indicators.note: only the inner letters of each word are kept, dropping the outer ones

blocks.note: the inner letters of clue
the inner letters of grids

explanation.surface: A solver's verdict on a dreadful puzzle and its grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid describes something shocking or gruesome, as in a lurid account.

clue.text: Permitted no whisper, we're told!

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: speaking aloud is the opposite of whispering

explanation.surface: A rule that bans whispering, so we hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowed and permitted are synonyms.

clue.text: Diary's regular date

indicators.note: regular means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A diary's usual appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A date in the calendar is a particular day.

clue.text: Gentle heating retains hot glow

indicators.note: something that retains holds on to it, keeping it inside

blocks.note: to simmer is to heat just below boiling
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A pan on a low heat keeps a warm glow.
explanation.definitionFit: To shimmer is to shine with a soft, wavering light.

clue.text: Ruhrland city's distinctive nature without church

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: the essence of something is its intrinsic nature
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A German industrial city loses its character when it has no church.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is a major industrial city in Germany's Ruhr valley.

clue.text: You once have to do wrong action. Absolutely

blocks.note: ye is an archaic form of you
to sin is to do wrong
a deed is an action

explanation.surface: Telling someone they once had to do something bad, then a firm affirmation.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic agreement, like saying 'certainly' or 'quite so'.
